universalAnswers.whatHappened: Reuters reported an inquiry into whether Nvidia structured its December Groq agreement to avoid antitrust scrutiny.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: The deal gave Nvidia permission to use Groq technology and moved senior Groq people to Nvidia while Groq remained independent.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Reuters supports the attributed inquiry and responses; Groq supports the announced deal structure.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The reporting does not establish wrongdoing, an outcome, remedy or consumer effect. A non-exclusive licence does not itself establish that Groq lost use, ownership or future licensing options.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: The story shows why competition questions can concern access to technology and expertise even without a whole-company purchase.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The reported inquiry concerns Nvidia, Groq and U.S. competition oversight; no reader-level price or product effect is established.
universalAnswers.changesNow: A formal request for information was reportedly sent; no liability finding is reported.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The department has not reported a conclusion, and Reuters attributed the inquiry details to the New York Times and two people.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Treat the inquiry as an open question and distinguish permission to use technology from ownership of the company or technology.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What permission did the licence grant and what did the hires change, if anything, while Groq remained independent?

legal-policy.legalStatus: A reported Justice Department inquiry with a formal information request, not a filing, ruling or judgment.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: The reported inquiry is by the U.S. Justice Department.
legal-policy.parties: Nvidia and Groq are the companies; the U.S. Justice Department is the reported investigator.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: Possible avoidance of antitrust scrutiny is the subject of the reported inquiry; no wrongdoing finding is reported.
legal-policy.currentEffect: The report establishes information-gathering, not a change for customers.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Whether the structure avoided scrutiny and what effect it had on competition remain unanswered.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: No dated next milestone is established; a department confirmation or conclusion would materially change the story.

company-business.businessChange: Nvidia received permission to use Groq inference technology and hired senior Groq people while Groq remained independent.
company-business.companyMotive: Nvidia says the agreement promotes innovation, rewards entrepreneurs and benefits consumers; other effects remain under reported inquiry.
company-business.payer: The sources used here do not establish a reliable deal value or reader payment.
company-business.beneficiary: Nvidia can use the licensed technology and hired experienced people; Groq says its company and GroqCloud continue.
company-business.incentives: The structure gives Nvidia technology access and experienced hires without transferring Groq ownership; the sources do not establish that Groq lost use of its technology.
company-business.customerEffectNow: No customer price, availability or performance change is established.

translation.newsVersionExact: Reuters reported on September 10 that the U.S. Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia structured its December agreement with AI chip startup Groq to avoid antitrust scrutiny.
translation.actualMeaningExact: An inquiry asks for answers; it is not a finding of wrongdoing.
translation.mechanismExact: Non-exclusive means Nvidia can use the technology; it does not by itself stop Groq from using it or licensing it to others.
translation.familiarExampleExact: “Not a takeover” describes the deal’s form. It does not answer what the licence and hires changed in practice.
